claims.text: The 2021 scoping review included 78 scientific studies of alleged past-life memories; 84% concerned children, 60% used case-report designs, 73% used interviews and 50% used documentary analysis.
provenance: peer-reviewed scoping review abstract and bibliographic record
limitations: These are characteristics of the published literature, not evidence that reincarnation itself is established.
claims.uncertainty: Publication and indexing choices may affect the represented literature base.

claims.text: In a 30-versus-30 Lebanese comparison study, children reporting past-life memories scored higher on daydreaming, attention-seeking and dissociation, but not on social isolation or suggestibility; dissociation scores were reported as non-clinical.
limitations: Small sample and observational design cannot establish cause.
The measured variables do not exhaust psychological or social explanations.
claims.uncertainty: The study constrains some simple psychological explanations but does not identify the origin of the reported memories.

claims.text: A 2024 case report described a child who made 13 statements about a deceased granduncle; investigators classified nine as correct and four as undetermined, and reported behavioral and anatomical correspondences.
limitations: Single retrospective family-linked case.
Correct matches do not uniquely establish the causal mechanism.
Information transfer, selective reporting and reconstruction must remain live alternatives unless independently excluded.
claims.uncertainty: The case is anomalous only to the extent that ordinary information pathways and reconstruction can be excluded; the abstract alone does not establish such exclusion completely.

claims.text: Reincarnation-type case literature contains reports with accurate biographical correspondences that some investigators interpret as potentially anomalous and relevant to mind-brain models.
provenance: peer-reviewed reviews by a field investigator
limitations: Anomalous correspondence is not equivalent to proof of reincarnation.
Field-investigator reviews are not independent replication.
claims.uncertainty: Multiple causal explanations can fit at least some reported cases; their relative adequacy varies case by case.

claims.text: For claimed past-life-memory cases, stronger inference requires early documentation of statements, separation of witnesses, explicit accounting of prior contacts and information pathways, prospective or blinded verification where feasible, and transparent reporting of both matches and misses.
limitations: Improved methodology can raise evidential quality but cannot guarantee a specific metaphysical conclusion.
claims.uncertainty: Some historical cases cannot be retrospectively upgraded to these standards because original documentation constraints are irreversible.

batch_conclusion.statement: Batch 3 establishes that a peer-reviewed observational literature exists around children reporting previous-life memories, including some documented biographical correspondences and psychological comparisons. The literature is methodologically heterogeneous and dominated by case reports, interviews and documentary analysis. It does not establish reincarnation as a proven mechanism, while simple psychological explanations assessed in some studies also do not explain every reported feature.
